newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says Britain's state borrowing on track.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says Britain's state borrowing on track.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Tuesday that Britain was on track, and may even do better than, its budget forecast for public finances.
Characterising public sector financing data on Tuesday as "excellent," Clarke said, "Today's figures are further confirmation that borrowing is on a clear downward path."
Clarke's comments were made in a statement read by a British Treasury official.
"We are now comfortably on track for the budget forecast and I am hopeful we will do even better than that," Clarke said in the statement.

Britain has a budget forecast for its public sector borrowing requirement of 26.4 billion pounds ($42.4 billion) for the year ending March 31, 1997 and a 19.2 billion projection for the year ending March 31, 1998.
